claims.text_en: Din Daeng is one of Bangkok's 50 khets, 8.354 km2, split into only two khwaeng: Din Daeng (4.618 km2, 68,251 people Dec 2023) and Ratchadaphisek (3.736 km2, 41,551; carved out of khwaeng Din Daeng on 26 July 2017 along Mit Maitri and Pracha Songkhro roads). Boundaries (Thai Wikipedia): north - Chatuchak along Khlong Bang Sue, Khlong Phraya Woek and Khlong Nam Kheaw; east - Huai Khwang along Ratchadaphisek and Asoke-Din Daeng roads; south - Ratchathewi along Khlong Sam Sen; west - Phaya Thai along Vibhavadi Rangsit Road. The khet was announced 8 Oct 1993 and took effect 14 January 1994, split from Phaya Thai; the name comes from the red laterite-dust road built in the 1940s under Field Marshal P. Pibulsongkram. Landmarks inside the app polygon (PIP-verified): BMA City Hall 2, University of the Thai Chamber of Commerce, the Stock Exchange of Thailand, Fortune Town, Jodd Fairs Ratchada, the Thailand Cultural Centre, Vibhavadi Rangsit Forest Park, and MRT Blue Line stations Phra Ram 9, Thailand Cultural Centre, Huai Khwang and Sutthisan. Outside the app polygon: MRT Phetchaburi and ARL Makkasan at the southern tip, the Esplanade and The Street Ratchada (across Ratchadaphisek in Huai Khwang), Saphan Khwai BTS, and the Army Sports Stadium.

question_answers.question: identity/scope
question_answers.answer: Khet Din Daeng, 8.354 km2, two khwaeng (Din Daeng 4.618 km2/68,251; Ratchadaphisek 3.736 km2/41,551 created 2017), bounded by Khlong Bang Sue (N), Ratchadaphisek + Asoke-Din Daeng roads (E), Khlong Sam Sen (S), Vibhavadi Rangsit Rd (W); khet effective 14 Jan 1994. App-polygon landmarks IN: City Hall 2, UTCC, SET, Fortune Town, Jodd Fairs Ratchada, Thailand Cultural Centre, Vibhavadi forest park, MRT Blue Phra Ram 9/Cultural Centre/Huai Khwang/Sutthisan. OUT: MRT Phetchaburi, ARL Makkasan, Esplanade, The Street Ratchada, Army Sports Stadium, Saphan Khwai BTS. Khwaeng-subarea claims marked partial.

question_answers.question: everyday experience
question_answers.answer: Two different halves: khwaeng Din Daeng is the flats-and-markets side (National Housing Authority flats, Din Daeng/Kwan Phatthana wet markets, City Hall 2, Vibhavadi forest strip), while khwaeng Ratchadaphisek is the transit-and-entertainment corridor (four MRT stations, Fortune Town, Jodd Fairs, Big C Extra, the Cultural Centre). Everyday life for residents runs through wet markets and sois; the corridor provides transit and evening economy. Partial by khwaeng.

question_answers.question: values+mechanisms
question_answers.answer: Transport 8 = four in-polygon MRT Blue stations on the eastern corridor (Phetchaburi/Makkasan cluster at the tip is outside the app polygon; no BTS inside; red-line missing link not built, ~2028 start reported). DE 9 = market-plus-mall density along one corridor. Rent 8 = mid-market portal pricing (1-bed 13-27k). Food 8 / nightlife 8 = 1,322 food + 85 nightlife POIs concentrating on Ratchada. Crowd 2 = Vibhavadi/Ratchadaphisek/expressway through-traffic plus top-tier density - and the noise record proves it.

question_answers.question: counter-evidence
question_answers.answer: Three: (1) Bangkok Index 2025 ranks Din Daeng last of 50 khets (17.35/50, down from 32nd) - the strongest published counter-signal to the app's positive scorecard; (2) the PCD noise record (71.6-81.6 dB(A), 182/182 days over standard) gives safety 5 its only objective physical correlate - environmental strain rather than crime; (3) green 8 cannot be reproduced from OSM named green (~3 ha vs app 15.5 ha).

question_answers.question: rhythm
question_answers.answer: Morning-evening commute pulses along Ratchadaphisek's four MRT stations and Vibhavadi's arterial flow; the evening economy (Jodd Fairs 17:00-01:00) concentrates on the corridor while the flat sois empty early; noise peaks with traffic - the monitoring data shows the standard is exceeded every single measured day, i.e. there is no quiet hour at the measurement point.

question_answers.question: walkability
question_answers.answer: Flat khet on a rectilinear grid; the market layer (Din Daeng, SRI Din Daeng, Kwan Phatthana markets) and the MRT stations line the two corridor roads, so everyday walking is block-scale along Din Daeng and Ratchadaphisek; crossing Vibhavadi and the expressway ramps is the hostile part. No walking durations were derived from catchment radius in this bundle.

question_answers.question: daily life
question_answers.answer: Daily needs: wet markets + Big C Extra + Fortune Town on the corridor; sports: Thai-Japanese Stadium, Wesn 2, Kheha fields, commercial gyms; transit: four MRT stations; evenings: Jodd Fairs strip. What the khet lacks is large green and quiet - the forest strip (08:00-18:00 dog-friendly) is the only substantial park.

question_answers.question: affordability vs stated figures
question_answers.answer: App 13,000/27,000 is consistent with HipFlat's portal data (studio avg USD385 ~13-14k THB, 1-bed USD446 ~15-16k, 2-bed USD710 ~25k; page-one 1-beds 13,090-27,000) given the khet's stock of older flats and mid-market condos; the trend is slightly negative (-6.3% vs Jan 2026). Rent 8 reads as 'cheap for the CBD-adjacent core', which the numbers support.

question_answers.question: green/quiet with polygon honesty
question_answers.answer: Green honesty: app 15.5 ha (1.8%) vs ~3 ha OSM named public green (Vibhavadi forest park 1.53 ha is the largest) - green 8 is generous unless the app counts road-planting/stadium grounds; coordinator methodology call needed. Quiet honesty: objectively the city's noisiest monitoring point (71.6-81.6 dB(A), 100% of days) - quiet is only found in interior soi blocks away from the corridors.

question_answers.question: conditional fit
question_answers.answer: Strong fit: commuters who live on the Ratchada corridor and want cheap-for-location rents with markets at the door and late-night food. Weak fit: anyone ranking quiet, park access, or environmental comfort first - the livability index and the noise record both point the other way; also weak for people who need BTS (there is none) or river access.

question_answers.question: recent changes 2024-2026
question_answers.answer: Jodd Fairs Rama 9 closed Jan 2025 and the consolidated Jodd Fairs Ratchada opened 1 Nov 2024 inside the khet; Bangkok Index livability fell to last place (2025); the 28 Jun 2026 BMC seat flipped to the People's Party; portal rents drifting down; SRT red-line missing link through the khet remains at planning/construction-start ~2028.

question_answers.question: uncertainties/outside-the-score
question_answers.answer: Unresolved: the park_ha 15.5 counting rule (OSM named green ~3 ha); the identity of the app's food/nightlife POI mix; safety 5 has no statistics (perception label recommended); TNN's 17.35 figure is snippet-corroborated only (article 403); the two planned-rail nodes (Orange/Grey 'Din Daeng', 'Pracha Songkhro') are construction-stage projects, not services; 'Soi Intharam 49' is Khaosod's transliteration and was not geolocated. Anchors verified against OSM with no mismatch.

preview.text_en: A two-speed khet: market-sois and housing blocks in khwaeng Din Daeng, and a four-station MRT strip with night markets on Ratchadaphisek - all under the city's loudest measured skyline of traffic.

guide_lead.text_en: Din Daeng packs city-hall offices, a top-tier daily-essentials layer and four MRT Blue Line stations into 8.35 km2 between Vibhavadi and Ratchadaphisek, with rents from the mid-teens - but it is also the district Bangkok's own livability index put last in 2025, and the Pollution Control Department's noisiest monitoring point (71.6-81.6 dB(A), every measured day over standard). Living here means corridor convenience with corridor noise, markets at the door, and a forest strip rather than a park.

strengths.text: Four in-polygon MRT Blue stations (Phra Ram 9, Cultural Centre, Huai Khwang, Sutthisan) give the khet a genuine rail spine without a BTS wait-list price.
Daily life is dense and cheap: wet markets plus Big C Extra and Fortune Town on the corridor, 1-bed rents of roughly 13-27k THB, and the Jodd Fairs night-market strip running 17:00-01:00.

tradeoffs.text: Objective environmental strain: the PCD's Din Daeng station is the city's noisiest (71.6-81.6 dB(A), 100% of measured days over the 70 dB(A) standard), and Rocket Media Lab's Bangkok Index 2025 ranks the khet last of 50 (17.35/50).
Green 8 overstates what the map shows: OSM named public green inside the khet sums to roughly 3 ha, led by the 1.53-ha Vibhavadi forest strip - the 15.5 ha app figure needs a methodology check.

day_night.text: Days run on civil-service and market rhythms around City Hall 2 and the wet markets; evenings shift to the Ratchadaphisek corridor (Jodd Fairs to 01:00) while the flat sois go quiet - with traffic noise never fully dropping, per the monitoring record.

within_area_variation.text: Khwaeng Din Daeng's flats-markets-schools half and khwaeng Ratchadaphisek's malls-stations-night-market half are effectively two neighbourhoods; the Phetchaburi/Makkasan transit cluster at the southern tip sits just outside the app polygon (batch-3's Makkasan khwaeng, Ratchathewi).

conditional_fit.text: Choose it if you want CBD-adjacent rents (13k studio / 25-27k 2-bed) with four MRT stations and 24-hour-grade food access, and can tolerate road noise as a constant.

Skip it if green space, quiet, or a BTS line matter most: the largest park is a roadside forest strip, the measured noise is the city's worst, and the livability index placed the khet 50th of 50 in 2025.

uncertainties.text: Unresolved: park_ha 15.5 counting rule (OSM named green ~3 ha); safety 5 has no published statistics (perception label recommended); the 17.35 livability score rests on snippet-corroboration (TNN 403); the red-line missing link through the khet is not under construction with a firm date. Anchors verified against OSM with no mismatch.

open_issues: park_ha 15.5 (1.8%) vs OSM named public green ~3 ha: gap plausibly = Vibhavadi planting strips + stadium grounds + unnamed BMA pocket parks; needs an app-methodology decision, not a data fix.
Safety 5: no district-level crime statistics found in EN or TH; the 2025 Khaosod items are organized-crime raids. Recommend a low-confidence/perception label.

Bangkok Index 17.35/rank-50 figure: TNN primary article is 403 (no bypass); corroborated only by search snippets + English Wikipedia's mention. Low confidence on the exact score; the last-place rank itself is corroborated by two families.
Thai Wikipedia's five-station MRT list includes 'Ratchadaphisek', which is not an operating Blue Line station name; treated as a slip - PIP-verified set is four stations.
Brief's 'st.phra-ram-9 catchment majority din-daeng (52.9%)' taken from batch-4 sibling bundle; not re-derived here.

App polygon excludes MRT Phetchaburi/ARL Makkasan at the southern tip while the brief credits them to the khet's edge - coordinator should reconcile transit-adjacency vs polygon membership for the transport score.
